The as-cast sample ( Fig. 2 (a)) exhibited the solidification microstructure comprising dendritic α -Al phases (dark contrast) surrounded by intermetallic phases with enriched alloy elements phases (bright contrast).
Such a dendritic cell structure was not observed in the solution-treated sample ( Fig. 2 (b)).
The XRD measurement for the solution-treated sample ( Fig. 3 ) revealed the presence of T-Al 6 Mg 11 Zn 11 [ 9 ], Al 3 (Ni, Cu) 2 [ 24 ], and α -Al phases.

Granular intermetallic phases with sizes of a few tens of micrometers (corresponding to the T-Al 6 Mg 11 Zn 11 and Al 3 (Ni, Cu) 2 phases) and relatively coarsened eutectic microstructures (including the remained Al 3 Ni phase) were distributed in the α -Al matrix in a non-uniform manner.
the diffraction peaks ( Fig. 3 ) derived from the Al 3 Ni phase [ 24 ] suggested that the Al 3 Ni phase would be locally formed in solidification and remain after the solution treatment at 480 ◦ C.
Apart from the T phase, the η -Zn 2 Mg phase containing Cu element preferentially precipitated on grain boundaries.
A large number of fine precipitates were dispersed homogeneously in the grain interior after the aging at 200 ◦ C or 300 ◦ C.
